title: Conditions of Use at the Till for the Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card
content:
The card is good only at approved retailers and only for the spending categories the tier allows; a transaction anywhere else is declined at the till rather than paid and recovered later. These are the conditions a transaction on a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card is measured against.

**Condition 1 — the programme is in use.** The programme stands at active on the day the transaction is authorised. The standing is read from the programme's own record before the transaction is authorised. A dormant, stopped or closed programme does not authorise a transaction.

**Condition 2 — the category and the size.** The retailer's spending category is one of the categories the tier makes the card good for, and the transaction is no larger than the tier's per-transaction maximum. The category, the amount and the retailer's name are read from the card entry for the transaction being authorised.

**Condition 3 — the category ceilings inside the period.** Each category the tier limits has its own ceiling inside the period: what is spent on over-the-counter items, on approved groceries and on utilities is counted separately, and a transaction that would pass one of those ceilings is declined even where the card still holds money. What is left of a period's allowance is the tier's quarterly allowance amount less what has been spent from the card so far in that period, and it is never less than nothing.

**Condition 4 — the transactions in a day.** A member may make only the tier's number of transactions in one day; a further attempt is declined for safety and released once the member confirms it was theirs.

**What is authorised.** The amount authorised on a transaction is the smallest of the amount presented, the tier's per-transaction maximum and the balance standing on the card.

**Cash.** The card is never good for cash, and a member asking to take cash out is told so plainly and offered the catalogue instead.

**Declines and unsettled authorisations.** A declined transaction is still recorded, with its reason, so that a member who says the card did not work can be told exactly what happened. A transaction that is authorised but never settled does not take money off the card, and a member who sees an authorisation fall away is told it was never a charge.
